excerpt: The integrated N-ethylcarbazole study reported 99.0% hydrogenation and 91.7% dehydrogenation with Pd-based catalysts under its optimized conditions.
Continuous NEC hydrogenation with 1 wt% Ru/Al2O3 reached 100% conversion, 99.41% selectivity to the fully hydrogenated product, and 5.79 wt% storage, at 80 °C and 4 MPa.

The toluene/MCH cycling study ran ten cycles. Toluene hydrogenation conversion exceeded 97% across all cycles. MCH dehydrogenation conversion fell from 90% to 84%. Demethylation and other byproducts occurred.
Guaiacol on Ru under H2 can undergo ring hydrogenation or competing hydrogenolysis of phenolic and ether C–O bonds; selectivity depends on the catalytic interface and hydrogen pressure.
Thermochemical analysis resolves methyl substitution effects in indole-based storage cycles. It does not rank catalytic reversibility or target-product selectivity of the candidates.
